newsitem.title: USA: Perot promises a "fair, paperless" tax system.
newsitem.headline: Perot promises a "fair, paperless" tax system.

text.p: Reform Party presidential candidate Ross Perot used a 30-minute paid infomercial on Sunday to call for the abolition of the Internal Revenue Service and sweeping reform of the U.S. tax code.
The Texas billionaire also proposed that any new tax increases be approved directly by voters.

"I pledge to you tonight that as your president we will get rid of the IRS and the tax code and replace them with a fair, paperless, modern system that will raise the revenues necessary to operate this great country," Perot said.
The television advertisement was aired on NBC-TV during prime-time viewing hours on Sunday.

Perot, running far behind President Bill Clinton and Republican nominee Bob Dole in the polls, blasted both candidates' positions on tax issues. He said Dole's proposed tax cut sounded good but did not make good business sense, and he criticized Clinton's proposal to cut capital gains taxes.
"I will not promise you free candy, because it is irresponsible," Perot said.
Perot called for a new, paperless tax system in his book "United We Stand" four years ago but stopped short of calling for abolition of the IRS at that time.
The businessman turned politician gained 19 percent of the vote in the 1992 presidential election, but his support has been running at only about 6 percent in recent polls.
He is expected to elaborate on his proposal in a speech to the Economic Club of Detroit on Monday.
Another Perot commercial will air on CBS-TV on Tuesday evening.
